title: What is Transfer Learning? 🧠
description: Learn the core idea of reusing pre‑trained weights to solve new problems with less data and time.

slides.title: Standing on the Shoulders of Giants 🏛️
slides.content:
# Transfer Learning in One Sentence

**Use a model already trained on a huge dataset (e.g., ImageNet) and adapt it to your own task.**

Instead of training millions of weights from scratch, you start with a network that already understands edges, shapes, and objects.

> Analogy: You want to become a pastry chef. You could learn cooking from scratch, or you could take a course that builds on your existing baking skills – much faster!

quizData.question: What is the main advantage of transfer learning?

options.text: It reduces the need for large datasets and long training times
It works without any training data

quizData.explanation: Transfer learning leverages learned features, so you need less data and fewer epochs to reach good performance.

slides.title: Why Train from Scratch is Hard 🧱
slides.content:
# Training a deep CNN from zero requires:
- Millions of labelled images.
- Days or weeks of GPU time.
- Careful hyper‑parameter tuning.

Most real‑world problems have only hundreds or a few thousand images. Transfer learning makes deep learning feasible for everyone.

slides.title: The ImageNet Legacy 🖼️
slides.content:
# The Gold Standard

ImageNet contains 1.2 million images across 1000 classes. Models trained on ImageNet have learned a rich hierarchy of visual features:
- **Early layers**: edges, colours, textures.
- **Middle layers**: shapes, patterns.
- **Later layers**: object parts, high‑level concepts.

These features are surprisingly generic and transfer well to other visual tasks.

slides.title: Transfer Learning vs Training from Scratch (Conceptual)
slides.codeSnippet:
# Training from scratch
model = create_my_cnn()
model.train(large_dataset, epochs=100)  # heavy

# Transfer learning
base_model = load_pretrained('VGG16')
model = add_classifier_head(base_model)
model.train(small_dataset, epochs=10)   # light

slides.title: Key Insight 💡
slides.content: Even if your task is very different from ImageNet (e.g., medical images), the low‑level features (edges, corners) are still useful. Transfer learning almost always beats training from scratch for image problems.
